title: Flowise executeJavaScriptCode -- T1611 caller-supplied nodeVMOptions spread overrides the sandbox's require allowlist
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-69254 (GHSA-3769-jgqc-cxm7),
affecting Flowise's `executeJavaScriptCode()` NodeVM sandbox.

`executeJavaScriptCode()` builds its sandbox options as
`{ ...defaultNodeVMOptions, ...nodeVMOptions }`, where
`defaultNodeVMOptions` restricts `require.builtin` to a safe
allowlist that blocks `child_process`, `fs`, and similar modules --
but `nodeVMOptions` is caller-supplied and spread AFTER the defaults,
so any key it sets silently overrides them. From inside a first,
correctly-sandboxed custom-function execution, an attacker requires
`flowise-components/dist/src/utils.js` by absolute path (bypassing
the module allowlist since the file is loaded, not required through
the restricted API), obtains a direct reference to
`executeJavaScriptCode()` itself, and calls it a second time with
`nodeVMOptions: { require: { builtin: ["*"] } }` -- re-enabling every
Node.js built-in inside the nested VM, including `child_process`.
Verified end-to-end against a stock `flowiseai/flowise` Docker image:
arbitrary commands execute as root, including reading
`/root/.flowise/encryption.key` (decrypts every stored credential)
and the JWT signing secret.

Detection logic flags a `POST /api/v1/node-custom-function` request
whose `javascriptFunction` body references
`flowise-components/dist/src/utils.js` together with
`nodeVMOptions` and a `require.builtin` override -- the exact
nested-sandbox-escape shape this advisory's proof of concept
confirms achieves root RCE against a live instance.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (FlowiseAI, via
GHSA, citing the exact source line for the vulnerable spread, a
7-step taint trace from route registration to RCE, and a fully
reproduced Docker-based exploit with proof-file and credential-file
read confirmation), fixed in Flowise 3.1.3 (verified via live GHSA lookup, 2026-09-04 -- the rule's original authoring predates the vendor's patch release; this note corrects a stale claim, not the detection logic itself).
